verdict.rationale: Clerky is a legal-paperwork platform, so a repository of executed contracts is a fair question to ask of it. The evidence shows a legal dashboard for doing more paperwork, change logs, and customizing key terms when drafting. None of this documents a searchable repository of executed contracts or automatic extraction of key terms and metadata. Entering key terms as drafting inputs is a different capability from extracting them from signed contracts.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, I can store executed contracts in a searchable repository with key terms and metadata extracted
